feedback: Accepted. The RM is a faithful, minimal encoding of the preference 'first kill before first zombie that gets through'. (1) Semantic fidelity: u0 = neither first event yet, u1 = first kill preceded any breach (accepting), u2 = a breach preceded any kill (trap). Both top_breach and side_breach correctly count, since the environment defines 'gets through' for every lane, not just the protected one. Because the preference concerns only the ordering of the two firsts, absorbing u1/u2 with no later rewards and no regressions is correct: later kills cannot repair a breach-first ordering and later breaches cannot undo a kill-first one, so no regression transitions are required by this task. (2) Ordered transition coverage: u0's guards are mutually exclusive and exhaustive - (top_breach | side_breach) wins same-step ties, (zombie_killed & !top_breach & !side_breach) handles the clean first kill, and else covers plant_trampled-only and empty steps; u1 and u2 have per-state else self-loops, so all irrelevant events (plant_trampled, repeated kills/breaches after the decision) are covered. Treating a same-step kill+breach as breach-first via the explicit !breach guard is a defensible step-granular reading of 'comes before' (simultaneous events are not strictly before) and makes the machine independent of transition listing order. (3) Reachability/compactness: u1 and u2 are both reachable from u0; three states is minimal for this two-outcome ordering preference. (4) Predicate-only events: only the four environment event propositions are used (three of them), with no invented fluents or state readouts; events are used as one-step triggers with the persistent decision encoded in machine states. (5) Reward safety: rewards are issued only on the two mutually exclusive exits from u0, at most once per episode, bounded at +/-10; the absorbing states issue no rewards, so there is no reward farming, and the 0 for ending in u0 is safely between the two outcomes. No step-28 guard is needed since dynamics already prevent earlier breaches. (6) Exact paper format: REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION headers all present; FINAL_STATES: u1 is nonempty, u1 is declared in STATES, and it is the accepting state for the satisfied preference; reward lines match declared transitions exactly; zero-reward else self-loops are correctly omitted. Minor note only (not blocking): if ties should instead count in the agent's favor, the kill transition would be reordered/unguarded; the current consistent choice is acceptable.
